items.title: Should animals be kept in zoos?
items.text:
Animal lovers often express indignation about how zoo animals lose their freedom, but I am of the opinion that animals should be kept in zoos.

Keeping animals in zoos offers a myriad of benefits, one of which is the chance for city dwellers to have encounters with animals in person. When people understand that animals aren’t just abstract entities that they only see in books and documentaries, they will be more inclined to want to safeguard animal welfare.

Another benefit is that many zoos actually play a leading role in animal conservation, thereby rescuing animals from the brink of extinction. The Singapore Zoological Gardens, for instance, channels a portion of its earnings towards region-wide conservation efforts, thereby safeguarding the populations of critically endangered species such as the sunda pangolin. If zoos play such an active role in animal conservation, we should support the keeping of animals in zoos.

Hello frens,

It seems like it’s been forever since I last wrote anything here.

Sometimes I get caught up in life, as most people do, and then on top of that, things happen that make it a bit more challenging like a heatwave, health stuff, or my cats taking turns howling at us right before we wake up and robbing us of that sweet, gentle morning. It happens.

But either way, I’m here, I’m giving it my best, and I’m quoting my good fren [Hildegard](https://samhainsam.art/2026/07/24/a-humble-servant-of-knowledge-hildegard-von-bingen/):

“...and so that, in the shipwreck of this world and in the heavy battles against iniquity, you may be an active and powerful knight, in order that you may shine like a bright star in eternal felicity.”

So I guess everything is already alright.

In that spirit, I’m here to present my newest project. It’s not exactly new-new, as you may recall, so I think it’s safer to call it an enhanced project: [RASPBERRARIUM!!!!!!!!! 🌱](https://stacker.news/items/1488464)

This idea had been floating around ever since I built it, and I finally got around to doing it.

But there’s a little story before this big step I took :P

At first, I wanted to add an LCD 1602 to it so it could show the moon phases, time, and so on. My tests were kind of okay, but at some point I think I burned the display while I was looking for code that fit it. I tried several versions until I found one that worked, but while I was trying to connect the cables to the right GPIOs, I made a mistake several times and on two occasions, but especially one, it started to smell like... burnt.

![](https://storage.ko-fi.com/cdn/useruploads/display/3f7702b5-8d9d-4eff-a489-b5826e67388f_img_8663.jpg)It worked... for a while

After that, it became kind of flaky and eventually stopped working altogether. Sigh.

Then I tried using the DHT sensor for humidity and temperature that came with the Pico kit, but I’m pretty sure that one was just bad quality. I looked into it and found that those sensors are cheaply made and quite fragile, so it’s very possible it wasn’t even my fault.

So you can guess I was a bit bummed out. But as I mentioned earlier, the heatwave was whipping my soul with its relentless evilness, and I just didn’t go back to the project for a while despite the initial excitement.

But alas! I persevered eventually and returned to it, and now it’s finally here.

I’m really happy with how it turned out.

I first tested the HDC1080 on its own, and it worked on the first try, which was a huge improvement compared to the previous sensor, where I had tried several codes and still got nothing.

items.title: Bitcoin is my Dread Pirate Roberts
items.text:
# Thank God for Bitcoin influenceoors

The influencer class in bitcoin is looking pretty bad right now...but I never would have learned half as much about Bitcoin without them. The podcasters (many of whom made their bread through sponsorships), the guide-writers, the dev personalities who have so much time for Twitter -- while it is true that [they are all scammers](https://nakamotoinstitute.org/mempool/everyones-a-scammer/), also couldn't help but teach me a little about Bitcoin.

As many bitcoiners describe, when I fell down the Bitcoin rabbit hole there wasn't a podcast I didn't listen to or a guide I didn't read. I tried out every wallet available at the time. I did IBD like seven times because I kept screwing up running an indexer on it and was so bad at computer stuff I didn't know how to keep my blocks data when I needed to try again. Like a child, the only way I could get some things done was if I want back to step zero and tried to follow the steps again. 

For all their attention-grabbing, don't-trust-verify hypocrisy, the clique of bitcoin cool kids managed to get me through a good number of levels. 

So when things like the Coldcard fuckup[^1] come out and all the influencers look like total chumps, I find that I can't be too mad at them because I don't know if I would have really gotten into bitcoin if it weren't for all their "content."

[^1]: I refer to it as the `Coldcard fuckup` because hack is really not the right word and while vulnerability may be the right word, it isn't strong enough.

# My sats aren't stolen yet

I still have my sats, and while I didn't get tripped up by this particular Coldcard blunder, I may end up falling for the next one...or making up one of my own. 

In the course of my time in Bitcoin I have had at least three major incidents where I thought I had completely screwed myself. These were good learning lessons. You can use testnet all you like, but it isn't until you are riding the high seas of mainnet that some things really hit home.

I know that I am not some shadowy supercoder. I'm still quite ignorant about many things in Bitcoin (getting Bitcoin details wrong is still pretty much a daily experience). I often am disappointed with how incredible my Bitcoin ignorance is. But dammit, it's so interesting, I can't seem to focus on anything else!

# Bitcoin is black market money

I've heard it said that Bitcoin may not be for normies, that if you don't need to transact in bitcoin, you probably shouldn't be messing around with it. This is a pretty sobering assessment.

I'm more like a normie than I'd like to admit. I'm a fairly unimportant person who hasn't even bought drugs with bitcoin or something mildly transgressive like that. I live in the US where the financial system works well enough and I can use e-trade if I want. I certainly don't do very much with black markets.

When I transact in bitcoin it's usually because I've gone out of my way to buy a cute coffee or something (well, except that I zap people all day long on SN and I currently don't know of any other platform that provides similar functionality sans sats...). And yet, I can't seem to get past bitcoin.

I don't know if normies should use bitcoin or not, but I still stand by the idea that Bitcoin is for anyone. It's incredibly easy to fuck it up, but if you want to use it, learn about it, try it -- don't let these fuckups stop you. You'll probably do something wrong and make a bunch of mistakes, but what else are you gonna do -- watch the next season of Survivor or something?  

# You don't become the Dread Pirate Roberts by staying home

One of the things that I most enjoyed writing on SN was the [True and Accurate History of Boating Accidents](https://stacker.news/items/869881). The conclusion I drew from researching that meme is that it's not your bitcoin unless you can fuck it up.

Here's something that didn't make it into that piece, but which nicely sums up the way I feel about self custody right now:

In *The Princess Bride* there's this moment where Wesley tells Buttercup about how the Dread Pirate Roberts would say to him every night:

"Goodnight, Wesley. Good work. Sleep well. I'll most likely kill you in the morning."

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aHZGqBVBCRw

Bitcoin is my Dread Pirate Roberts. It may kill me in the morning, but it's been a fine time for me.

Also, the no/low real estate and property tax expense is *insane*. I'm all in favor of establishments scrapping those bits but eeeh, doesn't really prove the efficiency of central planning then, does it?

> The city will provide the locations. That means low- or no-cost real estate, initial building support, and relief from rent and property taxes. So there will be a huge subsidy on that portion, and bids to run the stores will be judged on what subsidies are requested, but we don’t know the formula.

***

## "let’s take New York’s plan seriously and think through what we always think through."

> let’s start by assuming \[government-run grocery stores] are equally efficient.
> As always, start with the simple model. Imagine two stores. One private store becomes the government store, and the other remains private. Assume every household consumes a fixed grocery basket, so we’re not going to think about substitution across goods. Consumers are going to go to whoever supplies the cheaper basket relative to their transportation cost.

> We have core items whose prices are “forced” low and the rest of the items. Suppose half of the $100 on a normal trip is on those core items, and the city is going to tell the store to cut that by 30%. The dollar value of that portion falls to $35. If nothing else changes, the $100 trip now costs $85. Yay, everything is cheaper! The advertised 30% discount has produced a 15% discount overall. \[...] But the operator doesn’t sell a single product. It sells lots of products together. It’s going to raise prices on the non-core half until the total basket is back to $100.

> In that world, nothing has changed. Every basket is the same price. Shopping behavior is the same. Even if some staples look like they’ve changed, consumers are no better off in this world because what they actually care about is the bundle.

Everything is efficient, etc. NEXT:

> let’s relax the fixed-basket assumption. Suppose consumers are a little more responsive and non-core pricing isn’t going to undo the full discount, so the supported store’s total basket really does get cheaper. We can think of a variety of ways in which that happens. One possibility is that people shift toward the discounted core products, so the average bundle contains more goods with lower margins. The government store then has lower prices on average.

Enter competition, other stores shove down prices to (re-)attract customers

> Sounds great! Everyone gets cheaper groceries! People going to the government store get the larger reduction, while people who stay at the private store still benefit from the competition that has driven down its prices.
> we already know that these private stores have thin margins. With recurring fixed costs, it’s possible some are eventually driven out of business. In that case, this competitive pressure is weakened because the government store no longer has to compete with the private store. It can’t exercise its market power by raising prices on the core items, but it could still exercise its market power on all of those other goods.

## Subsidies... Subsidies EVERYWHERE

> Fixed contributions toward the site buildout and tax subsidies can help keep it operating, but they do not necessarily change the incentive to sell another basket.

> This really turns the pricing into something like a two-part tariff, where you have kind of a fixed cost part of the pricing, and then you have your marginal cost pricing on the goods. Think of Costco as one example. Costco collects a membership fee and then charges very low prices inside the store. Maybe this is essentially what New York will do, but instead of membership fees, that fixed cost is coming from the government.

Shocking

![](https://m.stacker.news/150539)

> They could be more efficient because they’ve been given a scale or a chance to reach a scale that’s generally not permitted in New York City. After all, New York City has kept out stores like Walmart, and these will presumably be five bigger stores. We also have all of the usual reasons for thinking that the stores would be less efficient.

Either the operator captures the gains...

> If you provide only a fixed-cost subsidy and let the operator maximize profits, then it has an incentive to be efficient. In that world, we go back to the case above, where most of the fixed subsidy is captured by the operator.

...or

> if the operator can’t maximize profit, or if the government claws back profits that it considers too high, then the incentive to minimize costs is weaker.

## "Letting the operator claim the gains from lower costs encourages efficiency, but it also lets the operator retain some of those gains rather than pass them through to consumers."

aaah, the waiting-in-line price:

> if there are still more shoppers than groceries, Barzel’s earlier work on [rationing by waiting](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/abs/10.1086/466785) tells us what comes next. Shoppers will then have to bid through another mechanism, in this case, bid with time. The line grows until the full price (price + waiting for simplicity), on the margin, is high enough to ration the available groceries. The market clears one way or another.

items.title: Makeshift cat shelter
items.text:
![](https://m.stacker.news/150697)

In the municipality where I live, there's a huge, empty lot (I don't know if it's private or state owned) where a makeshift cat shelter has sprung up. It wasn't originally intended as such, but little by little, it developed into a haven for cats. So far, 43 cats have been counted; some are born there, and others are abandoned. Honestly, that number seems low to me; judging by appearances, there appear to be many more. If you walk along nearby streets, you'll find at least three cats on every corner. No matter where you go, you'll see a stray cat.

![](https://m.stacker.news/150698)

Some people have access to this place and have built small shelters for the cats using recycled materials, so they can take refuge from the rain or the intense sun. People from the community also bring them food when they can.

Many were hiding inside those shelters, but at night it's incredible how the streets are filled with huge cats of all colors.

items.title: Bitcoin's BIP110 Moment: Three Possible Scenarios - Aaron van Wirdum
items.text:
This is a very nice and easy explainer of three possible scenarios of what happens in bitcoin the next few days. 

> **Scenario 1: (almost) no miners signal**
>  
> If current miner signaling is any indication, this is the scenario to expect.
>  
> From the perspective of anyone running Bitcoin Core or other non-BIP110 enforcing nodes and wallets (the vast majority of the Bitcoin ecosystem) blocks will be mined as usual, and transactions will be processed like normal too. Anyone who’s not actively tracking these events on social media or elsewhere may not even be aware that anything unusual is going on, and in a practical sense for them there really won’t be; BIP110 does not affect them.
>  
> The same is not true for anyone running Bitcoin Knots or other BIP110-enforcing nodes, however. Since their software will reject non-signaling blocks, they basically wouldn’t see any new blocks at all (or perhaps a few per week), and incoming and outgoing transactions won’t confirm (or incredibly slow). In practical terms, these nodes would stall and become unusable.
>  
> If this happens, BIP110 proponents will have to decide between waiting to see if things improve for them (see scenario 3), giving up (switching back to non-BIP110 software), or deploying a next protocol change, like hard forking to a different proof-of-work mining algorithm.

items.title: Conditional Message Transfer Contract To Solve Jamming
items.text:
> **Abstract**. In this post, we present the prolegomenas for a formalization to a new mitigation paradigm of the channel jamming, a cheap of denial-of-service attack affecting the Lightning Network.
>
> Our proposed mitigation relies on leveraging the bitcoin script capabilities, in its present state, to allow channel counterparties to unequivocally agree off-chain that a deterministic message has been previously exchanged or not among them at a given blockchain time, a practical universal clock.
>
> This proof of message transfer constitutes a wider solution to the channel jamming attack, where counterparties should be able to decide for how long a HTLC or PTLC has been withheld over a channel and to charge fees in consequence.
>
> **Introduction**. A brief informal re-statement of the problem.
>
> “*The holy grail? is indeed charging fees as a function of the time the HTLC was held. As for now, we are not aware of a reasonable way to do this. There is no universal clock, and there is no way for me to prove that a message was sent to you, and you decided to pretend you didn’t. It can easily happen that the fee for a two-week unresolved HTLC is higher than the fee for a quickly resolving one*”.

items.title: What the heck is a spawn camping attack in Bitcoin?
items.text:
# BIP110ers are super cereal

You may have seen Chris Guida's post a few days ago where he noted that he had prepared Luke Dashjr's older proof-of-work-change code for use "just in case miners decide to collude to betray bitcoin." https://stacker.news/items/1540163

Although the move was quickly seconded by most of the bip110 crew (Mechanic, Dathon Ohm, Kratter, and Dashjr himself), Dathon [assured](https://x.com/dathon_ohm/status/2084893307616829543) me that the code would only be used in an "unlikely contingency"

![](https://m.stacker.news/151064)

# What's the point of changing the proof of work algorithm?

Bitcoin mining relies on a specific math function (SHA256). Bitcoin miners use circuit boards designed to compute SHA256 on 80 byte Bitcoin block headers and they are pretty good at it, but they are not so good at computing other functions. So, if a chain wanted to stop all the large-scale miners from attacking it, they might decide to use a different function to compute the proof of work for new blocks.

One possible alternative to SHA256 could be RIPEMD160. Large-scale Bitcoin miners who had invested lots of money in ASICs would not be in a very good position to mine blocks on a blockchain requiring proof of work via RIPEMD160. This is what people mean when they refer to "firing the miners."

Again, the BIP110ers assure me that this is not a likely outcome and that they are only preparing the code out of an abundance of caution and that they are super, super cereal.

# Out of the pot and into the Spawn Camping Attack fire

However, in the very surprising scenario where most of the Bitcoin world ignores BIP110 and they find themselves forked off on a small, minority chain with very little hashrate, it seems possible that they would opt to change the proof of work algorithm rather than be exposed to 51% attacks.

Should they make such a change, it is possible that they would be opening themselves up to a different sort of attack: one that Vitalik Buterin [dubbed](https://x.com/VitalikButerin/status/827783678910558208) the Spawn Camping Attack.

![](https://m.stacker.news/151065)

Michael Tidwell [described](https://x.com/miketwenty1/status/2084740955261878491) this attack as:

> This is when there are no asics for a given mining algo, so any motivated attacker with large access to gpu's can just keep sniping the new chain with the new algo no matter how many times you change it.

You might say it's kind of like a powerful player camping out next to a spawn point in a FPS game and killing everyone the second they spawn.

Keeping in mind that GPUs seem to be easier (if not cheaper) to rent than they were back in 2017, you could see a world where the BIP110ers change their proof-of-work algo, and immediately get 51% attacked by whoever is willing to rent enough GPUs to do it. Jumping to a new algorithm (firing the miners) doesn't work anymore though because wihtout ASICs, all algos are equally equally efficient for all players.

There are probably other ways of dealing with this sort of attack, but it would be interesting to see if something like this plays out.

items.title: A tough guy, a dog, and the end of the world: The perfect combination?
items.text:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-xSxaE1ClEE

Well, yesterday I got a notification about a trailer, and when I started watching it, wow! It blew me away. Ridley Scott with a post-apocalyptic horror film? How is that even possible? I know he has dystopian worlds and aliens under his belt, but not in that straightforward style, as far as I knew. I watched it, and since I'm a fan of that style of film and television, I recognized the formula immediately.

Post-apocalyptic cinema has taught us that when society collapses and humanity shows its worst side, there's no better lifeline than an armed spirit, a desolate horizon, and, of course, a four-legged companion.

![](https://m.stacker.news/151112)

The recent trailer and previously unseen footage of The Dog Stars, directed by the legendary Ridley Scott, confirm that this time-tested formula remains the undisputed queen of survival on the big screen. With a cast led by [Jacob Elordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Elordi) and [Josh Brolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Brolin), the film promises, I'm almost certain, to become the new benchmark for this subgenre.

***

# What the trailer reveals

Based on [Peter Heller's acclaimed book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dog_Stars), the story takes place nine years after a brutal global pandemic wiped out almost all of humanity.

In this devastated landscape, we meet Hig (Jacob Elordi), a skilled widowed pilot who survives in isolation in an airplane hangar (a rather common location for this type of setting, haha) in Colorado. His only allies in this void are his loyal dog and Bangley (Josh Brolin), a former naval operative, armed to the teeth and an expert in military survival tactics.

The trailer exudes a suffocating atmosphere of high tension. We see the enormous complicity—but also the ideological clash—of this unlikely duo. While protecting their perimeter from the lethal "reapers" (ruthless looters), a mysterious radio transmission awakens a spark of hope in Hig, (a common theme in these kinds of films).

This compels him to start his small plane and embark on a perilous journey into the unknown, crossing that invisible line that gives the film its title—the same old story: leaving the safe haven for the insecure. But what can you do?

***

# The Infallible Formula: Cinematic Relatives

For those of us who love stories where a solitary man finds solace in an animal while dodging extinction, Ponto Sem Retorno feels like coming home. It's impossible not to draw direct parallels with the genre's great pillars:

**I Am Legend:** The purest reflection of loneliness. Will Smith and his dog Samantha showed us that canine loyalty is the only thing that keeps a man sane amidst the silence of the end of the world.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IVG3D1JlQ2Q

**Mad Max 2:** The Road Warrior: The original road warrior already traveled the wasteland with an Australian Cattle Dog and a shotgun, defending gasoline trucks from looters.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rV9m_iHe7gA

**The Walking Dead:** The great Daryl Dixon and his beloved Dog (a beautiful Belgian Malinois whose real name was Seven) are one of the best modern examples.

https://www.youtube.com/shorts/-a30jfSscvc

**Dawn of the Dead:** In this Zack Snyder classic, an adorable Border Collie named Chips becomes the hero of a key scene. Since zombies ignore animals and only seek human flesh, survivors use it to send supplies through the horde.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hl8ZjY5vTbI

***

# The Ridley Scott Signature: A Guaranteed Success

![](https://m.stacker.news/151109)

If the premise of "a tough guy and his dog" is already appealing, the name behind the camera raises expectations to astronomical levels. Ridley Scott is an undisputed master of cinematic atmosphere. To speak of him is to speak of the visual majesty of Blade Runner, the claustrophobic tension of Alien, and the epic pulse of Gladiator or Black Hawk Down.

![](https://m.stacker.news/151110)

With a screenplay by [Mark L. Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_L._Smith) ([The Revenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Revenant_(2015_film))) and the impeccable, textured cinematography of [Erik Messerschmidt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_Messerschmidt), we know beforehand that every shot of this devastated world will be a work of art. Scott constructs worlds that feel painfully real, barren, and dangerous, worlds that are always the envy of other directors, I'm almost certain.

The premiere of this post-apocalyptic "odyssey" is scheduled for the end of August in theaters.

![](https://m.stacker.news/151113)

I think with this gathering of actors, producers, directors, etc., the film looks promising. I'm definitely going to sit here and wait for it, ready with my popcorn.

items.text:
I've seen lately a lot of posts about x and y wanted to fork Bitcoin for whatever reason.
And always came to my mind [this old warning post from Mircea Popescu](http://trilema.com/2015/if-you-go-on-a-bitcoin-fork-irrespective-which-scammer-proposes-it-you-will-lose-your-bitcoins/), on Jan 06, 2015.
Here is a copy of it:

---

Some random scammer[^1], pretending great import and high office in Bitcoin like all the scammers coming before him[^2] (all of which the hostile eye of the mainstream media, as well as the dim, unseeing eye of the mass "follower" presented as actually important, for a brief time, back in the day - and generally for pay) is going to create a "Bitcoin killer".

Unlike the MtGox coins, Aurora coins, Etherium coins, Ripple coins, Paycoins and whatever other scammy "better than Bitcoin", "Bitcoin replacement" etc peddled to date, the current scammer is brasher in his attempt (as scammers are wont to be, they call this "being innovative" on their dedicated scammer forums), and he actually claims to be seriously involved in Bitcoin development, at the behest of a fake "Bitcoin Foundation". These claims are both false, on the strength of the historical record, and both are squarely rejected by the actual Bitcoin Foundation.

What's left is the nude reality of the matter : if you, either misguided by some scammer's malice, or simply through ignorance, actually modify your Bitcoin client to accept the nonconformant transactions, the result will be that any Bitcoin you hold will be slowly (or perhaps not so slowly, depending on your use habits) replaced by worthless scam-Bitcoins, that will not be accepted by the main players in Bitcoin anymore than they'd accept something you've drawn yourself.

The fate of this fork will be exactly the fate of all attempted forks to date[^3] : the savvy Bitcoin holders will sell their fake-Bitcoins on the fake network, while double-spending (and thus invalidating) their sale on the actual network, thereby keeping their actual Bitcoin safe[^4] . 

The proceeds of this "victimless"[^5] crime will be used to purchase more legitimate Bitcoins on the legitimate network, thus draining away value from the holders of Bitcoin fakes, into the pockets of the legitimate Bitcoin holders. Which of these two do you wish to be... well... now that you consider the matter, it's pretty obvious, right ? Certainly, not all will consider the matter, but if your morals are in their right place you will at least let them know, if you can get to them.

To make it perfectly clear : in no case will MPEx accept this fake Bitcoin, as it's not accepted any other fake Bitcoin to date, and for the exact reasons. Moreover, my budget to sink this scam exceeds the budget of everyone involved on the supporting side[^6]. That is all.

[^1]: One Gavin Andresen, known principally for his costumed clown services, where he goes to various conferences dressed as this or that for the amusement of the participants.

[^2]: Trendon Shavers thought he was very important, [Mark Karpeles](http://trilema.com/2013/any-questions/) thought he was very important, [Max Keiser](http://trilema.com/2013/in-which-noobs-learn-lessons-and-pay-for-the-privilege/) thought he was very important, Andreas Antonopoulous thought he was very important before his untimely death, Vitalik Buterin thinks he is very important, Josh Garza thinks he is very important, the list is [endless](http://trilema.com/2013/the-story-of-pointless-and-witless/).

[^3]: That all miserably failed, needless to say, to a chorus of lulzy stuff like ![](https://m.stacker.news/71015)

[^4]: The reverse is not possible, by the way : this scammer's fork is, as designed, forced to accept transactions on the legitimate Bitcoin network, but the legitimate network could never accept transactions based on movements on the fork.

[^5]: In the sense that its only victims are the gullible idiots empowering a scammer, something you're never ever supposed to do, by the way. Note that this is not the first time when "everyone" supported a scammer, and when "the consensus" seemed to be that nonsense is now quite sensible. This did exactly nothing to alleviate the 100% loss of those involved - whose voices you do not hear precisely because that is the fate of the gullible, the scammer following crowd.

items.title: Should animals be kept in zoos?
items.text:
Animal lovers often express indignation about how zoo animals lose their freedom, but I am of the opinion that animals should be kept in zoos.

Keeping animals in zoos offers a myriad of benefits, one of which is the chance for city dwellers to have encounters with animals in person. When people understand that animals aren’t just abstract entities that they only see in books and documentaries, they will be more inclined to want to safeguard animal welfare.

Another benefit is that many zoos actually play a leading role in animal conservation, thereby rescuing animals from the brink of extinction. The Singapore Zoological Gardens, for instance, channels a portion of its earnings towards region-wide conservation efforts, thereby safeguarding the populations of critically endangered species such as the sunda pangolin. If zoos play such an active role in animal conservation, we should support the keeping of animals in zoos.

Bitfinex \~119,756 BTC (hack, 2016)

BlockFi \~77,000 BTC (insolvency, 2022)
Quadriga \~76,000 BTC (CEO's death, 2019)
Voyager \~65,000 BTC (insolvency, 2022)

Coldcard \~1,500 BTC

Coldcard accounted for 0.081% of the amount lost by exchanges.
For every bitcoin lost due to this bug, custodians lost over 1,200 BTC.

The error is avoidable: diversify, use multisig, create your own entropy, and never put your BTC on a CEX. The data speaks for itself—though, as my grandmother used to say, nobody learns from others' mistakes.

Hello frens,

It seems like it’s been forever since I last wrote anything here.

Sometimes I get caught up in life, as most people do, and then on top of that, things happen that make it a bit more challenging like a heatwave, health stuff, or my cats taking turns howling at us right before we wake up and robbing us of that sweet, gentle morning. It happens.

But either way, I’m here, I’m giving it my best, and I’m quoting my good fren [Hildegard](https://samhainsam.art/2026/07/24/a-humble-servant-of-knowledge-hildegard-von-bingen/):

“...and so that, in the shipwreck of this world and in the heavy battles against iniquity, you may be an active and powerful knight, in order that you may shine like a bright star in eternal felicity.”

So I guess everything is already alright.

In that spirit, I’m here to present my newest project. It’s not exactly new-new, as you may recall, so I think it’s safer to call it an enhanced project: [RASPBERRARIUM!!!!!!!!! 🌱](https://stacker.news/items/1488464)

This idea had been floating around ever since I built it, and I finally got around to doing it.

But there’s a little story before this big step I took :P

At first, I wanted to add an LCD 1602 to it so it could show the moon phases, time, and so on. My tests were kind of okay, but at some point I think I burned the display while I was looking for code that fit it. I tried several versions until I found one that worked, but while I was trying to connect the cables to the right GPIOs, I made a mistake several times and on two occasions, but especially one, it started to smell like... burnt.

![](https://storage.ko-fi.com/cdn/useruploads/display/3f7702b5-8d9d-4eff-a489-b5826e67388f_img_8663.jpg)It worked... for a while

After that, it became kind of flaky and eventually stopped working altogether. Sigh.

Then I tried using the DHT sensor for humidity and temperature that came with the Pico kit, but I’m pretty sure that one was just bad quality. I looked into it and found that those sensors are cheaply made and quite fragile, so it’s very possible it wasn’t even my fault.

So you can guess I was a bit bummed out. But as I mentioned earlier, the heatwave was whipping my soul with its relentless evilness, and I just didn’t go back to the project for a while despite the initial excitement.

But alas! I persevered eventually and returned to it, and now it’s finally here.

I’m really happy with how it turned out.

I first tested the HDC1080 on its own, and it worked on the first try, which was a huge improvement compared to the previous sensor, where I had tried several codes and still got nothing.

![](https://storage.ko-fi.com/cdn/useruploads/display/c67aebd0-cf93-442b-833e-83199f1fa7e2_img_86122.jpeg)

Then the next step was incorporating it into the existing code for my Raspberrarium. After a few tries and some vibecoding, it was possible. I also had to change the SDA and SCL pins from their original positions in the code to different GPIO pins, because the original pin assignment conflicted with the rest of the circuit.

![](https://storage.ko-fi.com/cdn/useruploads/display/f612e40f-1709-4d7b-9e64-3e039defbce0_img_3617.jpg)

But I wanted to take it a step further, as I had mentioned I wanted to see the humidity, temperature, and moon phase without having to connect it to my computer and since that’s not possible via SSH, I still had an option: making a webpage with the sensor values and moon phases. 🤯 

After some tweaking and making it as pinkish as I wanted, it finally turned out great.

Of course, I can only visit it while I’m at home, but that’s totally fine. I was only going to be able to see the LCD at home anyway, so that’s a win in my book.

I’m very, very happy with how it turned out, and not a day goes by when I’m not in awe of this beauty.

As usual, I also had help from my amazing husband, who helped solder the HDC1080 and make a kind of bridge so the Pi’s GND could be used by the LEDs, the HDC1080, and the Pi itself.

![](https://storage.ko-fi.com/cdn/useruploads/display/7870f936-0bdf-4ff9-9369-6d32e4ab5983_img_8642.jpeg)

Yay, so that’s basically it and yes, you can tell I’m quite happy about it.

As usual, wishing you all the best, stay safe and take care.

# Thank God for Bitcoin influenceoors

The influencer class in bitcoin is looking pretty bad right now...but I never would have learned half as much about Bitcoin without them. The podcasters (many of whom made their bread through sponsorships), the guide-writers, the dev personalities who have so much time for Twitter -- while it is true that [they are all scammers](https://nakamotoinstitute.org/mempool/everyones-a-scammer/), also couldn't help but teach me a little about Bitcoin.

As many bitcoiners describe, when I fell down the Bitcoin rabbit hole there wasn't a podcast I didn't listen to or a guide I didn't read. I tried out every wallet available at the time. I did IBD like seven times because I kept screwing up running an indexer on it and was so bad at computer stuff I didn't know how to keep my blocks data when I needed to try again. Like a child, the only way I could get some things done was if I want back to step zero and tried to follow the steps again. 

For all their attention-grabbing, don't-trust-verify hypocrisy, the clique of bitcoin cool kids managed to get me through a good number of levels. 

So when things like the Coldcard fuckup[^1] come out and all the influencers look like total chumps, I find that I can't be too mad at them because I don't know if I would have really gotten into bitcoin if it weren't for all their "content."

[^1]: I refer to it as the `Coldcard fuckup` because hack is really not the right word and while vulnerability may be the right word, it isn't strong enough.

# My sats aren't stolen yet

I still have my sats, and while I didn't get tripped up by this particular Coldcard blunder, I may end up falling for the next one...or making up one of my own. 

In the course of my time in Bitcoin I have had at least three major incidents where I thought I had completely screwed myself. These were good learning lessons. You can use testnet all you like, but it isn't until you are riding the high seas of mainnet that some things really hit home.

I know that I am not some shadowy supercoder. I'm still quite ignorant about many things in Bitcoin (getting Bitcoin details wrong is still pretty much a daily experience). I often am disappointed with how incredible my Bitcoin ignorance is. But dammit, it's so interesting, I can't seem to focus on anything else!

# Bitcoin is black market money

I've heard it said that Bitcoin may not be for normies, that if you don't need to transact in bitcoin, you probably shouldn't be messing around with it. This is a pretty sobering assessment.

I'm more like a normie than I'd like to admit. I'm a fairly unimportant person who hasn't even bought drugs with bitcoin or something mildly transgressive like that. I live in the US where the financial system works well enough and I can use e-trade if I want. I certainly don't do very much with black markets.

When I transact in bitcoin it's usually because I've gone out of my way to buy a cute coffee or something (well, except that I zap people all day long on SN and I currently don't know of any other platform that provides similar functionality sans sats...). And yet, I can't seem to get past bitcoin.

I don't know if normies should use bitcoin or not, but I still stand by the idea that Bitcoin is for anyone. It's incredibly easy to fuck it up, but if you want to use it, learn about it, try it -- don't let these fuckups stop you. You'll probably do something wrong and make a bunch of mistakes, but what else are you gonna do -- watch the next season of Survivor or something?  

# You don't become the Dread Pirate Roberts by staying home

One of the things that I most enjoyed writing on SN was the [True and Accurate History of Boating Accidents](https://stacker.news/items/869881). The conclusion I drew from researching that meme is that it's not your bitcoin unless you can fuck it up.

Here's something that didn't make it into that piece, but which nicely sums up the way I feel about self custody right now:

In *The Princess Bride* there's this moment where Wesley tells Buttercup about how the Dread Pirate Roberts would say to him every night:

"Goodnight, Wesley. Good work. Sleep well. I'll most likely kill you in the morning."

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aHZGqBVBCRw

Bitcoin is my Dread Pirate Roberts. It may kill me in the morning, but it's been a fine time for me.

items.title: Comrade Mamdani and His Pretty Good Grocery Stores (Economic Forces, Albrecht)
items.text:
**Aha, and so it begins!**

TL;DR:

> I still think this will end up displaying all the normal reasons to think a municipal grocery store is a dumb idea: bad pricing incentives, inefficient transfers, and all that stuff. At the end of the day, we can’t eliminate trade-offs and scarcity. This is a competitive industry. The discount is unlikely to come purely out of profits.

(I routinely find myself not having much to say about these *excellent* **Economic Forces** pieces... comprehensive and thorough as is... no Den snark needed)

![](https://m.stacker.news/150244)

(uh-hu? Yea... I believe you. Good luck sourcing enough quantity... and *rationing access*...)

> Who pays for the discount? What are the equilibrium responses? Where does adjustment occur when it cannot occur in the prices of those 20 items? Let’s think through the usual stuff: competition, transactions costs, fixed vs. marginal decisions.

Also, the no/low real estate and property tax expense is *insane*. I'm all in favor of establishments scrapping those bits but eeeh, doesn't really prove the efficiency of central planning then, does it?

> The city will provide the locations. That means low- or no-cost real estate, initial building support, and relief from rent and property taxes. So there will be a huge subsidy on that portion, and bids to run the stores will be judged on what subsidies are requested, but we don’t know the formula.

***

## "let’s take New York’s plan seriously and think through what we always think through."

> let’s start by assuming \[government-run grocery stores] are equally efficient.
> As always, start with the simple model. Imagine two stores. One private store becomes the government store, and the other remains private. Assume every household consumes a fixed grocery basket, so we’re not going to think about substitution across goods. Consumers are going to go to whoever supplies the cheaper basket relative to their transportation cost.

> We have core items whose prices are “forced” low and the rest of the items. Suppose half of the $100 on a normal trip is on those core items, and the city is going to tell the store to cut that by 30%. The dollar value of that portion falls to $35. If nothing else changes, the $100 trip now costs $85. Yay, everything is cheaper! The advertised 30% discount has produced a 15% discount overall. \[...] But the operator doesn’t sell a single product. It sells lots of products together. It’s going to raise prices on the non-core half until the total basket is back to $100.

> In that world, nothing has changed. Every basket is the same price. Shopping behavior is the same. Even if some staples look like they’ve changed, consumers are no better off in this world because what they actually care about is the bundle.

Everything is efficient, etc. NEXT:

> let’s relax the fixed-basket assumption. Suppose consumers are a little more responsive and non-core pricing isn’t going to undo the full discount, so the supported store’s total basket really does get cheaper. We can think of a variety of ways in which that happens. One possibility is that people shift toward the discounted core products, so the average bundle contains more goods with lower margins. The government store then has lower prices on average.

Enter competition, other stores shove down prices to (re-)attract customers

> Sounds great! Everyone gets cheaper groceries! People going to the government store get the larger reduction, while people who stay at the private store still benefit from the competition that has driven down its prices.
> we already know that these private stores have thin margins. With recurring fixed costs, it’s possible some are eventually driven out of business. In that case, this competitive pressure is weakened because the government store no longer has to compete with the private store. It can’t exercise its market power by raising prices on the core items, but it could still exercise its market power on all of those other goods.

## Subsidies... Subsidies EVERYWHERE

> Fixed contributions toward the site buildout and tax subsidies can help keep it operating, but they do not necessarily change the incentive to sell another basket.

> This really turns the pricing into something like a two-part tariff, where you have kind of a fixed cost part of the pricing, and then you have your marginal cost pricing on the goods. Think of Costco as one example. Costco collects a membership fee and then charges very low prices inside the store. Maybe this is essentially what New York will do, but instead of membership fees, that fixed cost is coming from the government.

Shocking

![](https://m.stacker.news/150539)

> They could be more efficient because they’ve been given a scale or a chance to reach a scale that’s generally not permitted in New York City. After all, New York City has kept out stores like Walmart, and these will presumably be five bigger stores. We also have all of the usual reasons for thinking that the stores would be less efficient.

Either the operator captures the gains...

> If you provide only a fixed-cost subsidy and let the operator maximize profits, then it has an incentive to be efficient. In that world, we go back to the case above, where most of the fixed subsidy is captured by the operator.

...or

> if the operator can’t maximize profit, or if the government claws back profits that it considers too high, then the incentive to minimize costs is weaker.

## "Letting the operator claim the gains from lower costs encourages efficiency, but it also lets the operator retain some of those gains rather than pass them through to consumers."

aaah, the waiting-in-line price:

> if there are still more shoppers than groceries, Barzel’s earlier work on [rationing by waiting](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/abs/10.1086/466785) tells us what comes next. Shoppers will then have to bid through another mechanism, in this case, bid with time. The line grows until the full price (price + waiting for simplicity), on the margin, is high enough to ration the available groceries. The market clears one way or another.

items.title: Makeshift cat shelter
items.text:
![](https://m.stacker.news/150697)

In the municipality where I live, there's a huge, empty lot (I don't know if it's private or state owned) where a makeshift cat shelter has sprung up. It wasn't originally intended as such, but little by little, it developed into a haven for cats. So far, 43 cats have been counted; some are born there, and others are abandoned. Honestly, that number seems low to me; judging by appearances, there appear to be many more. If you walk along nearby streets, you'll find at least three cats on every corner. No matter where you go, you'll see a stray cat.

![](https://m.stacker.news/150698)

Some people have access to this place and have built small shelters for the cats using recycled materials, so they can take refuge from the rain or the intense sun. People from the community also bring them food when they can.

Many were hiding inside those shelters, but at night it's incredible how the streets are filled with huge cats of all colors.

items.title: Bitcoin's BIP110 Moment: Three Possible Scenarios - Aaron van Wirdum
items.text:
This is a very nice and easy explainer of three possible scenarios of what happens in bitcoin the next few days. 

> **Scenario 1: (almost) no miners signal**
>  
> If current miner signaling is any indication, this is the scenario to expect.
>  
> From the perspective of anyone running Bitcoin Core or other non-BIP110 enforcing nodes and wallets (the vast majority of the Bitcoin ecosystem) blocks will be mined as usual, and transactions will be processed like normal too. Anyone who’s not actively tracking these events on social media or elsewhere may not even be aware that anything unusual is going on, and in a practical sense for them there really won’t be; BIP110 does not affect them.
>  
> The same is not true for anyone running Bitcoin Knots or other BIP110-enforcing nodes, however. Since their software will reject non-signaling blocks, they basically wouldn’t see any new blocks at all (or perhaps a few per week), and incoming and outgoing transactions won’t confirm (or incredibly slow). In practical terms, these nodes would stall and become unusable.
>  
> If this happens, BIP110 proponents will have to decide between waiting to see if things improve for them (see scenario 3), giving up (switching back to non-BIP110 software), or deploying a next protocol change, like hard forking to a different proof-of-work mining algorithm.

items.title: Conditional Message Transfer Contract To Solve Jamming
items.text:
> **Abstract**. In this post, we present the prolegomenas for a formalization to a new mitigation paradigm of the channel jamming, a cheap of denial-of-service attack affecting the Lightning Network.
>
> Our proposed mitigation relies on leveraging the bitcoin script capabilities, in its present state, to allow channel counterparties to unequivocally agree off-chain that a deterministic message has been previously exchanged or not among them at a given blockchain time, a practical universal clock.
>
> This proof of message transfer constitutes a wider solution to the channel jamming attack, where counterparties should be able to decide for how long a HTLC or PTLC has been withheld over a channel and to charge fees in consequence.
>
> **Introduction**. A brief informal re-statement of the problem.
>
> “*The holy grail? is indeed charging fees as a function of the time the HTLC was held. As for now, we are not aware of a reasonable way to do this. There is no universal clock, and there is no way for me to prove that a message was sent to you, and you decided to pretend you didn’t. It can easily happen that the fee for a two-week unresolved HTLC is higher than the fee for a quickly resolving one*”.

items.title: What the heck is a spawn camping attack in Bitcoin?
items.text:
# BIP110ers are super cereal

You may have seen Chris Guida's post a few days ago where he noted that he had prepared Luke Dashjr's older proof-of-work-change code for use "just in case miners decide to collude to betray bitcoin." https://stacker.news/items/1540163

Although the move was quickly seconded by most of the bip110 crew (Mechanic, Dathon Ohm, Kratter, and Dashjr himself), Dathon [assured](https://x.com/dathon_ohm/status/2084893307616829543) me that the code would only be used in an "unlikely contingency"

![](https://m.stacker.news/151064)

# What's the point of changing the proof of work algorithm?

Bitcoin mining relies on a specific math function (SHA256). Bitcoin miners use circuit boards designed to compute SHA256 on 80 byte Bitcoin block headers and they are pretty good at it, but they are not so good at computing other functions. So, if a chain wanted to stop all the large-scale miners from attacking it, they might decide to use a different function to compute the proof of work for new blocks.

One possible alternative to SHA256 could be RIPEMD160. Large-scale Bitcoin miners who had invested lots of money in ASICs would not be in a very good position to mine blocks on a blockchain requiring proof of work via RIPEMD160. This is what people mean when they refer to "firing the miners."

Again, the BIP110ers assure me that this is not a likely outcome and that they are only preparing the code out of an abundance of caution and that they are super, super cereal.

# Out of the pot and into the Spawn Camping Attack fire

However, in the very surprising scenario where most of the Bitcoin world ignores BIP110 and they find themselves forked off on a small, minority chain with very little hashrate, it seems possible that they would opt to change the proof of work algorithm rather than be exposed to 51% attacks.

Should they make such a change, it is possible that they would be opening themselves up to a different sort of attack: one that Vitalik Buterin [dubbed](https://x.com/VitalikButerin/status/827783678910558208) the Spawn Camping Attack.

![](https://m.stacker.news/151065)

Michael Tidwell [described](https://x.com/miketwenty1/status/2084740955261878491) this attack as:

> This is when there are no asics for a given mining algo, so any motivated attacker with large access to gpu's can just keep sniping the new chain with the new algo no matter how many times you change it.

You might say it's kind of like a powerful player camping out next to a spawn point in a FPS game and killing everyone the second they spawn.

Keeping in mind that GPUs seem to be easier (if not cheaper) to rent than they were back in 2017, you could see a world where the BIP110ers change their proof-of-work algo, and immediately get 51% attacked by whoever is willing to rent enough GPUs to do it. Jumping to a new algorithm (firing the miners) doesn't work anymore though because wihtout ASICs, all algos are equally equally efficient for all players.

There are probably other ways of dealing with this sort of attack, but it would be interesting to see if something like this plays out.

items.title: A tough guy, a dog, and the end of the world: The perfect combination?
items.text:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-xSxaE1ClEE

Well, yesterday I got a notification about a trailer, and when I started watching it, wow! It blew me away. Ridley Scott with a post-apocalyptic horror film? How is that even possible? I know he has dystopian worlds and aliens under his belt, but not in that straightforward style, as far as I knew. I watched it, and since I'm a fan of that style of film and television, I recognized the formula immediately.

Post-apocalyptic cinema has taught us that when society collapses and humanity shows its worst side, there's no better lifeline than an armed spirit, a desolate horizon, and, of course, a four-legged companion.

![](https://m.stacker.news/151112)

The recent trailer and previously unseen footage of The Dog Stars, directed by the legendary Ridley Scott, confirm that this time-tested formula remains the undisputed queen of survival on the big screen. With a cast led by [Jacob Elordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Elordi) and [Josh Brolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Brolin), the film promises, I'm almost certain, to become the new benchmark for this subgenre.

***

# What the trailer reveals

Based on [Peter Heller's acclaimed book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dog_Stars), the story takes place nine years after a brutal global pandemic wiped out almost all of humanity.

In this devastated landscape, we meet Hig (Jacob Elordi), a skilled widowed pilot who survives in isolation in an airplane hangar (a rather common location for this type of setting, haha) in Colorado. His only allies in this void are his loyal dog and Bangley (Josh Brolin), a former naval operative, armed to the teeth and an expert in military survival tactics.

The trailer exudes a suffocating atmosphere of high tension. We see the enormous complicity—but also the ideological clash—of this unlikely duo. While protecting their perimeter from the lethal "reapers" (ruthless looters), a mysterious radio transmission awakens a spark of hope in Hig, (a common theme in these kinds of films).

This compels him to start his small plane and embark on a perilous journey into the unknown, crossing that invisible line that gives the film its title—the same old story: leaving the safe haven for the insecure. But what can you do?

***

# The Infallible Formula: Cinematic Relatives

For those of us who love stories where a solitary man finds solace in an animal while dodging extinction, Ponto Sem Retorno feels like coming home. It's impossible not to draw direct parallels with the genre's great pillars:

**I Am Legend:** The purest reflection of loneliness. Will Smith and his dog Samantha showed us that canine loyalty is the only thing that keeps a man sane amidst the silence of the end of the world.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IVG3D1JlQ2Q

**Mad Max 2:** The Road Warrior: The original road warrior already traveled the wasteland with an Australian Cattle Dog and a shotgun, defending gasoline trucks from looters.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rV9m_iHe7gA

**The Walking Dead:** The great Daryl Dixon and his beloved Dog (a beautiful Belgian Malinois whose real name was Seven) are one of the best modern examples.

https://www.youtube.com/shorts/-a30jfSscvc

**Dawn of the Dead:** In this Zack Snyder classic, an adorable Border Collie named Chips becomes the hero of a key scene. Since zombies ignore animals and only seek human flesh, survivors use it to send supplies through the horde.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hl8ZjY5vTbI

***

# The Ridley Scott Signature: A Guaranteed Success

![](https://m.stacker.news/151109)

If the premise of "a tough guy and his dog" is already appealing, the name behind the camera raises expectations to astronomical levels. Ridley Scott is an undisputed master of cinematic atmosphere. To speak of him is to speak of the visual majesty of Blade Runner, the claustrophobic tension of Alien, and the epic pulse of Gladiator or Black Hawk Down.

![](https://m.stacker.news/151110)

With a screenplay by [Mark L. Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_L._Smith) ([The Revenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Revenant_(2015_film))) and the impeccable, textured cinematography of [Erik Messerschmidt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_Messerschmidt), we know beforehand that every shot of this devastated world will be a work of art. Scott constructs worlds that feel painfully real, barren, and dangerous, worlds that are always the envy of other directors, I'm almost certain.

The premiere of this post-apocalyptic "odyssey" is scheduled for the end of August in theaters.

![](https://m.stacker.news/151113)

I think with this gathering of actors, producers, directors, etc., the film looks promising. I'm definitely going to sit here and wait for it, ready with my popcorn.
